title: Relations among sets
competency: Describe relationships among sets: equal, equivalent, subset and proper subset.

keywords.def: Two sets with exactly the same elements. A = B.
Two sets with the same number of elements. A ↔ B.
A ⊆ B when every element of A is also in B.
A ⊂ B when A ⊆ B and B has at least one element that is not in A.
A drawing that shows sets as circles.

en.text: Two sets are equal when they have exactly the same elements. Order and repetition do not matter. {p, q, r, s} = {q, r, p, s}, and {1, 1, 2, 2, 3} = {1, 2, 3}.

screens.title: Same or different?
screens.ask: A = {p, q, r, s} and B = {q, r, p, s}. Are A and B the same set?
screens.after: They have exactly the same elements. Order does not matter in a set. So A = B.

screens.title: A. Equal sets
paras: Definition 1.2: Two non-empty sets A and B are equal if they have exactly the same elements. We write A = B.
table: A = {p, q, r, s}, B = {q, r, p, s}

screens.title: Key words
defs: Two sets with exactly the same elements. A = B.

screens.why: Both sets have exactly 2, a and 4.
screens.clue: Check each element. Does order matter?

screens.why: c is only in the first set and d only in the second.
screens.clue: Is every element in both sets?

screens.why: Repeats do not count. Both sets are {5, 6}.
Equal sets have exactly the same elements. 4 and 9 are in both, so x must be 7.
screens.clue: Which element of the second set is missing from the first?

en.text: Two sets are equivalent when they have the same number of elements. {5, 7, 9} and {x, y, z} both have 3 elements, so they are equivalent. Equal sets are always equivalent, but equivalent sets need not be equal.

screens.title: What is the same?
screens.ask: {5, 7, 9} and {x, y, z} share no element. What do they have in common?
screens.after: Both have 3 elements. Sets like this are called equivalent.

screens.title: B. Equivalent sets
paras: Definition 1.3: Sets A and B are equivalent, written A ↔ B, if they have an equal number of elements.
table: A = {p, q, r, s}, B = {q, r, p}
screens.note: All equal sets are equivalent, but not all equivalent sets are equal.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Two sets with the same number of elements. A ↔ B.

screens.text: All equivalent sets are equal sets.
screens.why: {1, 2} ↔ {a, b}, but they do not have the same elements.

screens.title: Equal, equivalent or neither?
screens.why: Equal: same elements. Equivalent: same number of elements.
screens.clue: First count, then compare the elements.

screens.text: A = the whole numbers less than 4. Which set is equivalent to A but NOT equal to A?
screens.why: A = {0, 1, 2, 3} has 4 elements. {1, 2, 3, 4} also has 4, but its elements differ. {0, 1, 2, 3} and {3, 2, 1, 0} are equal to A.
screens.clue: Write A first. Then look for 4 elements that are not the same.

en.text: A is a subset of B, written A ⊆ B, when every element of A is also in B. The empty set is a subset of every set, and every set is a subset of itself. The subsets of {1, 2} are { }, {1}, {2} and {1, 2}.

screens.title: Inside another set
screens.ask: A = {2, 3, 5} and B = {2, 3, 5, 7, 9}. Is every element of A also in B?
screens.after: 2, 3 and 5 are all in B. So A is inside B. We say A is a subset of B.

screens.title: A inside B
screens.ask: Tap a circle, then tap each number.
rings: {2, 3, 5}: every element is also in B.
numbers: In A, so also in B.
In A, so also in B.

screens.title: C. Subsets
paras: Definition 1.4: A is a subset of B if every element of A is also an element of B. We write A ⊆ B.
A = {a, c, e} is not a subset of B = {a, e, i, o, u}, because c ∉ B. We write A ⊄ B.

screens.title: Note
paras: 1. The empty set is a subset of any set: { } ⊆ A.
2. Any set is a subset of itself: A ⊆ A.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A ⊆ B when every element of A is also in B.

screens.why: 2 is in the first set but not in {6, 8}.
screens.clue: Check every element of the first set.

screens.why: The empty set is a subset of any set.

screens.text: A = {0, b}. Tap every subset of A.
screens.why: Subsets: { }, {0}, {b} and {0, b}. 1 is not in A.
screens.clue: Use no element, one element, then both.

screens.ask: How many subsets does {a, b, c} have? ___
screens.clue: List them by size: 0, 1, 2 and 3 elements.

en.text: A is a proper subset of B, written A ⊂ B, when A ⊆ B and B has at least one element that is not in A. A set is not a proper subset of itself. In a Venn diagram, a proper subset is a circle inside a bigger circle.

screens.title: Itself?
screens.ask: Is {a, c} a proper subset of {a, c}?
screens.after: A set is a subset of itself, but never a proper subset of itself. A proper subset must leave something out.

screens.title: D. Proper subsets
paras: Definition 1.5: A is a proper subset of B, written A ⊂ B, if A ⊆ B and B has at least one more element.
A = {a, e, c} and B = {a, c, d, e}: every element of A is in B, and d is extra. So A ⊂ B.

screens.title: Note
paras: 1. The empty set is a proper subset of any other set: { } ⊂ A, if A is not empty.
2. No set is a proper subset of itself: A ⊄ A.
The proper subsets of {a, c} are {a}, {c} and ∅.

screens.title: Venn diagrams
paras: A Venn diagram shows a set as a circle. The elements go inside the circle.
A = {1, 4, 5} and B = {1, 4, 5, 6}. A ⊂ B, so circle A is drawn inside circle B. 6 is in B but outside A.

screens.title: A ⊂ B as a Venn diagram
numbers: Only in B: this makes A a proper subset.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A ⊂ B when A ⊆ B and B has at least one element not in A.
A drawing that shows sets as circles.

screens.why: 7 and 4 are in the bigger set, and 5 and 6 are extra.
screens.clue: Is A inside B, with something left over?

screens.why: The two sets are equal. A set is not a proper subset of itself.
screens.clue: Does the second set have any extra element?

screens.text: B = {m, 2}. Tap every proper subset of B.
screens.clue: Proper subsets leave out at least one element.

screens.text: M = {0, 4, 6, 8} and N = {6, 8}. Which Venn diagram is right?
opts: Two circles that do not touch
screens.why: 6 and 8 are in M, so N ⊂ M. N goes inside M; 0 and 4 sit in M outside N.
screens.clue: Is every element of N in M?

screens.text: A ⊆ B and B ⊆ A. What must be true?
screens.why: Every element of A is in B and every element of B is in A. So they have exactly the same elements: A = B.
screens.clue: If each set is inside the other, what can you say?

items.why: Every element of the first set is in the second.
They are equal sets. A set is not a proper subset of itself.
The empty set is a proper subset of any non-empty set.

items.text: Let A = {0, b}. List all subsets of A.
items.clue: Include the empty set and A itself.

items.text: E = {a, x, m, 4} and F = {a, 4, 8, 9}. Which Venn diagram fits?
opts: Two overlapping circles: a and 4 in the middle
Two circles that do not touch
items.ans: Two overlapping circles: a and 4 in the middle
items.why: a and 4 are in both. x, m are only in E; 8, 9 only in F.
items.clue: Which elements are in both sets?

items.why: Equal sets have the same elements, so the same number of elements.
items.clue: Same elements means the same count.

items.text: A set is a proper subset of itself.
items.why: No set is a proper subset of itself.

items.text: If A = B, then A ⊆ B.
items.why: Every element of A is in B.
items.clue: Any set is a subset of itself.

test.why: Same elements; order does not matter.

test.text: Which set is equivalent to {p, q, r}?

test.why: 3 and 5 are both in the second set.

test.text: Tap every proper subset of {x, y}.
test.why: {x, y} itself is not a proper subset.
It has 8 subsets; leave out the set itself: 8 − 1 = 7.

notes.text: Example 2 prints {1,2,3, } with a stray comma; shown as {1, 2, 3}. Example 11 prints B = {a, c, d, e, }; shown as {a, c, d, e}.
Examples 3–4 print F = {x, , u, 3} (an empty slot). Read as F = {x, u, 3}, which Example 4 needs (3 elements). Teacher to confirm.
Example 13 writes ∅ ⊆ A in a list of proper subsets; it should be ∅ ⊂ A.
The Venn note on p.7 says A = {1, 5, 6} but the drawing shows 1, 3 and 2. Not used in the lesson.
Definition 1.5 says "B has at least one more element"; the lesson explains it as "an element that is not in A".
Venn diagrams with one circle inside another use the nest block; the student cannot draw circles, so Exercise 1.2.1 Q4–Q5 are asked as multiple choice.
